summary: Eugen Pander was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga (~1873–1876) and served at Tongwen Guan in 1881 as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German.
Eugen Prym worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at the University of Bonn from around 1860 to 1865 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1869 to 1913.

Eugen Wilhelm specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under August Schleicher (~1862–1866) and served as a professor at the University of Jena from around 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Obermiller specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1921–1935) and held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1927–1935) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1930–1935).

Eugene Watson Burlingame specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman in 1909 and held appointments at the University of Pennsylvania (~1908–1913), Johns Hopkins University (~1914–1917), and Yale University (~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield (~1992–1997), and held posts at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997) and Harvard University (~1997).
Eugeni d'Ors was a philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona (~1898–1903) and Universidad Central (~1903–1905). He later held a post at Universidad Central from around 1927 to 1936.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Lviv (~1919–1926), later holding posts there (~1928–1941), at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~1945–1953), and at the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian studies. He studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1822–1832) and held positions at the Société Asiatique (1826, 1829, 1832), Collège de France (1832–1852), and Imprimerie Nationale (~1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet was an Indologist and linguist. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from around 1828 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from around 1832 to 1838.

Eugène Tisserant worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Lycee Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1904–1908), and the École du Louvre (~1905–1908).

Eun Hino is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2006). She served as a project researcher at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2014) and assistant professor at Musashino University (~2014).
Keiun Maeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Kōzui Ōtani. Over the course of his career, he served as president of both Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini, and held posts at the University of Michigan (until 2004) and Seoul National University (2004).
Eunyoung Choe is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate from Korea University. She was attested as an HK Professor at Geumgang University between 2013 and 2015.

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 2006, she was attested as a professor emeritus at the University of Alberta and Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.
Eva Neumaier-Dargyay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin and held a post at the University of Calgary.

Eva Tichy is a linguist and Indologist. She studied under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1974–1981), completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg (~1981–1989), and held the chair of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Freiburg (1993–2017).

Eva Wilden is an Indologist who earned her degrees and habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1986–2003). She held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (2003) and the University of Hamburg (2017).

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College under Robert A. F. Thurman and at the University of Toronto, also studying with Francisco Varela. His posts include York University (2002–2005), University of Toronto (2005), and UBC (2013).
